ops.title: service: launchctl bootstrap EIO on wedged Aqua-session label — no bootout-and-retry recovery
ops.description:
Field evidence (local machine, 2026-07-25, captain-hook 12.20.10 brew post-install): daemonkit's service install path failed with

```
service: install agent "com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper": launchctl bootstrap:
  worker: process exited with code 5: Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error
  (launchd EIO after 6 attempts; desired session "Aqua", current manager "Aqua")
```

The label was wedged — neither loaded (`launchctl list` absent) nor cleanly re-bootstrappable — and daemonkit retried bootstrap 6× against the same wedged state, then gave up, leaving brew's post-install failed and the helper down. The standard launchd recovery for this state is `bootout` (tolerating "not loaded") followed by a fresh `bootstrap`; the v0.20.x work added exit-113 (not-loaded) handling and stale-program heal, but persistent bootstrap EIO has no bootout-first recovery rung.

Suggested shape: on repeated `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` for a label whose desired and current session domains match, attempt exactly one bootout (ignoring not-loaded) and one final bootstrap before surfacing the error. Keep it bounded — no loops.

Related field context: the failure left captain-hook's deployed app stale while `capt-hook helper install` later reported success (separate captain-hook bug, filed in that repo's backlog — false-success on skipped redelivery). A logout/login also clears wedged Aqua labels, which is the manual remedy the error message could name.

ops.text: reproduce or unit-simulate a wedged-label bootstrap EIO and demonstrate the bootout-then-bootstrap recovery converges it
service install surfaces a wedged-label failure with the manual remedy named when recovery fails
captain-hook post-install on a machine with a wedged helper label converges instead of failing
